title: Bibliography: Every Source the Book Cites
basis: Reconstructed on 2026-11-13 from the published page (posts/bibliography/index.md, generated by _research/bib-tools/run.sh) and its former spec.md, whose Non-goals, Decision log, Sources and Changelog are carried over. One spec paragraph per unit of the page in its order; each topic's entry list is one paragraph with form list. Intent, acceptance criteria and role are copied unchanged from journal-spec.json; the journal spec gives a reference page no thesis, so the thesis here is the page's own and only orders its sections. A light pass for a lookup page: entries were checked for consistency, not rewritten.

know: Every public source the pages cite, listed once with a stable R-number, date, evidence type, the claim it supports and the pages citing it, by topic and by chapter.
believe: A claim is as trustworthy as the kind and age of its source: a law records a requirement, a filing reported numbers, API documentation an interface as read, an engineering post what a company said it built that year.
can_do: Trace a figure or rule in a chapter to its dated source and weigh it by evidence type and date.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader traces a claim in chapter 46 to its source and says how widely the book relies on it.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Using only this page: chapter 46 says Shopify retries a failed webhook delivery 8 times over 4 hours. Which entry stands behind it, what kind of evidence is it, when was it read, and how many pages cite it?
acceptance_criteria.expected: R409, Shopify: Webhooks, Shopify developer documentation, undated (n.d.) and accessed in November 2026; product and API documentation; it supports duplicate and unordered deliveries and 8 retries over 4 hours, and is cited in 12 pages, case-shopify among them.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader weighs a source by its type and date.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Using only this page: a 2016 engineering post describes a company's architecture, and a documentation page is marked 'n.d.'. How far should a reader trust each for a claim about today, and does any source describe Kestrel & Pine?
acceptance_criteria.expected: An engineering post records what a company said it built in that year; an old architecture post describes its period, not necessarily the present system. 'n.d.' means undated, so the access month (November 2026) shows when the documentation was read. No source describes Kestrel & Pine, which is fictional; labeled inferences and recommendations are the author's judgement.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader of the introduction alone (the callouts and the paragraphs before the first section heading) can predict what the page contains and the kind of evidence or material it uses.
acceptance_criteria.probe: After reading only the introduction: what will this page give you, in what order, and from what kind of material?
acceptance_criteria.expected: A register that traces each claim to its source and shows when that evidence was published or checked, researched in November 2026, with 'n.d.' meaning undated; some sources in Dutch, German, French or Polish; Productscape models listed once as planning material, not evidence; then how to read the register (R-numbers identify, do not rank; stable identifiers), a topic index, entries by topic and sources by chapter.

thesis.question: Which sources does the book cite?
thesis.claim: The book cites 847 public sources, each listed once with a stable R-number, its date, its evidence type, the claim it supports and the pages citing it, by topic and by chapter; a claim is as trustworthy as the kind and age of its source, and no source describes Kestrel & Pine.
thesis.disputed_by: The view that a reader can follow a chapter's own Sources section or search the web, so a consolidated register adds nothing.
thesis.so_what: A reader traces any figure or rule to a dated document, weighs it by evidence type and age, and sees how many pages rely on it.
thesis.how_why: The register is generated from every page's Sources and Evidence section with stable identifiers, consolidating equivalent URLs and keeping the most specific date.

supporting_claims.claim: An entry is identified by a stable R-number and carries its date, evidence type, supported claim and citing pages.
Every cited source can be found by topic or by citing chapter, and weighed by its evidence type and date.

role.contribution: Closes the book's apparatus: every cited source once, so any claim can be traced to a dated document by topic or by chapter.

flow.rationale: How to read an entry comes first, because every entry is weighed by its type and date; the topic index then maps the topics before the entries themselves; the by-chapter list reads the same sources from the citing side, and the closing ends the reference pages.

hook.content: Use this register to trace a claim in any chapter to its public source and see when that evidence was published or checked.

bridge.from_reader_world: The reader has met a figure, a rule or a company fact in a chapter and wants to know what stands behind it.
bridge.to_topic: Every cited source is gathered here once, with its date and evidence type, by topic and by chapter.

thesis_statement.text: Sources are listed because they were cited; their dates and evidence types tell you how far to trust a claim; documented facts, inferences and Kestrel & Pine stay distinct.

roadmap.placement: IN THIS SECTION callout and paragraphs p01-p02 (the by-chapter lookup, in the conclusion region, is also announced there)

promises.promise: How to read an entry (R-number, fields, evidence type).
A topic index, then the entries by topic.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Use the register to trace a claim to its source and its date, by topic or by chapter; research took place in November 2026 and 'n.d.' means undated, so the access month dates the reading.
The page first explains how to read an entry, then gives a topic index, the entries by topic and the sources by chapter (some sources being in other languages).

conclusion.heading: Sources by Chapter
conclusion.synthesis: The four reference pages answer the four lookups a chapter leaves the reader with (where, which record, what word, what source), and each answer points back to the chapter that owns it.
conclusion.so_what: A claim, a term or a card in any chapter can be checked against its owning chapter and its dated source without rereading the book, and a disagreement between them is a defect to fix.

callback.to: This page's KEY POINTS: weigh a claim by the kind and age of its source; keep documented facts, inferences and Kestrel & Pine apart.
callback.how: The closing turns them into the course of action for using the whole book, and, as the Reference part's closing, recalls domain-coverage's opening point that the book does not cover every job equally.

takeaway.content: Before relying on a figure or a rule from the book, find its source in the register, check the source's type and date, and keep documented facts, labeled inferences and Kestrel & Pine apart.

transition_in.introduces: The same sources read from each citing page.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Each citing page lists the identifiers it cites, in reading order.
No source describes Kestrel & Pine, which is fictional, and the recommendations, labeled inferences and assumptions are the author's judgement.

transition_in.introduces: What no source stands behind.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The four reference pages answer four lookups that point back to the owning chapter, so check coverage and a claim's source, type and date before relying on it.

transition_in.introduces: The close of the reference pages.

non_goals.topic: A reading list, a ranking of sources, the research briefs, the plan or links to companion books

open_questions: Before print: the Amazon SP-API links on the host developer-docs.amazon (R132, R337, R344–R347, cited from pricing-architecture, customer-service-and-notifications and marketplaces-and-channel-integration) were reported broken by one reader and could not be checked offline on 2026-11-13; if the host does not resolve, change those chapters' links to developer-docs.amazon.com and rerun run.sh.

decision_log.decision: Draft check, round 1 (ESCALATE, 8 pass, 11 fail, none waived). Readers run: one cold reader each for AC-1 and AC-2 on the whole page; AC-3 on the introduction only; a reverse outliner on all 35 units with each long list cut to its first six lines; two flow readers on a sample (introduction, How to Read, Topic Index in full, first five entries of each topic list and of Sources by Chapter, and the closing); a judge on the spec, structure output and those answers. The other checks were judged from that sample, not from every entry. After the round, cheap fixes were made without a second round: a roadmap sentence in the introduction (AC-3), the Productscape sentence moved to How to Read (two readers), a sentence explaining the non-contiguous ranges and two placement-rule wordings in the Topic Index (two readers), a contrast opening for the Kestrel & Pine line, the coverage-page callback linked; in the spec, p02's controlling idea, the roadmap promises and callback.to (auto-resolved by the author's standing instruction of 2026-11-12: spec follows the readers' corroborated moves; rejected: leaving the spec's two-caveat paragraph and the off-page callback). check-report.json is therefore stale against these edits.

Converted spec.md to spec.json in a light pass for a lookup page: one spec paragraph per draft unit, each topic's entry list one list paragraph; the thesis is the page's own because the journal spec gives a reference page none. length.max_words is the published length plus 10% (32,751 words as check_draft counts them; 36,026).
rejected: Carrying the old inventory-style success criteria over: each (entries come from Sources sections; entry fields; topics follow the parts; stable R-numbers; generated page) describes contents or process, not a reader outcome, and the journal spec's three acceptance criteria replace them

decision_log.decision: Added the Reference part's closing as one short paragraph at the end of the page (p33), as the journal spec's reference part closing says, and made the first prose sentence say what the page is for and how to use it.
rejected: Placing the closing before the Kestrel & Pine note
